studies.title: Loud & Clear 2026
studies.claim: For another year, Spotify was the highest-paying retailer globally, paying the music industry more than $11 billion in 2025 and bringing our all-time total to nearly $70 billion.

source.label: Spotify newsroom, Loud & Clear 2026 highlights post (Mar 11, 2026); company-reported, not in the 20-F
source.quote: For another year, Spotify was the highest-paying retailer globally, paying the music industry more than $11 billion in 2025 and bringing our all-time total to nearly $70 billion.

ecosystem.notes: The 20-F states no total for royalties paid to rights holders (cost of revenue consists predominantly of royalty and distribution costs related to content streaming, but royalties are not broken out), so payouts is null. The study figure is Spotify's own from its Loud & Clear 2026 report, in US dollars (the filing reports in euros), stated as 'more than $11 billion', so 11 is a lower bound; it is money paid to the music industry as a whole (rights holders such as labels and publishers, not only artists). It is not audited filing data. It replaces the Loud & Clear 2025 figure ($10 billion for 2024). No volume measure exists, so measure is null.

notes: Ecosystem lens only. The Loud & Clear figure is stored under studies because it is company-reported and in USD, while the filing is in EUR.
